source_notes.text: Dataset provenance: rows 2–149 are the 148 supplied records, retained unchanged; their real-world provenance was not independently verified. Rows 150–1001 are 852 computer-generated synthetic innings, appended in this same sheet. They do not report actual performances by the named players. No separate data sheets or source columns were added.

Generation method: seeded match-block resampling of the supplied 25 match groups. Seed 26102026, LCG (1664525,1013904223). Player IDs, formats, innings and dismissal/line/length/shot/bowler tuples are inherited jointly from a sampled match. Runs and balls are perturbed with bounded random variation; strike rate is recalculated to 2 decimal places. New match IDs begin at 26. Dates are simulated from 01/01/2023, four days apart, and are not verified fixtures. Template match IDs are recorded in notes on each added match. This augmentation adds no independent real observations. Split original matches before augmentation, generate training-only augmentation, and evaluate on untouched verified real matches. Do not use a random split of this combined sheet to claim real-world accuracy.

Researcher-defined rule-based INNINGS performance labels, added 26 October 2026. These are not coach assessments, validated cricket standards, or recent-form ratings.

Apply rules in this order within each format:
T20: Poor if Runs < 15; Good if Runs >= 30 AND strike rate >= 120; Average otherwise.
ODI: Poor if Runs < 20; Good if Runs >= 50 AND strike rate >= 80; Average otherwise.
Test: Poor if Runs < 20; Good if Runs >= 50; Average otherwise. Test strike rate is not used.

For classification, strike rate is calculated as 100 * Runs / Balls Faced, using unrounded values. A zero-ball innings is assigned strike rate 0 for the rule; a zero-run run-out is Poor as a scoring outcome, with no inference about technique. Existing Strike Rate values are retained unchanged. Not-out status, batting position and match situation do not change this simplified rating.

These labels were assigned automatically and consistently using the stated rubric. They describe single innings, not the player's current form. Training on the same runs and strike rate used to define these labels measures reproduction of the rubric, not independent coaching quality. For forecasting, use earlier-innings features only. Existing source/synthetic provenance notes remain applicable. Keep synthetic records out of the final verified-real test set.

grouping: Source-match families from existing notes, falling back to Match ID; grouping columns are never model inputs.
date_policy: Day-first text parsed explicitly; existing Excel date values retained. No inferred date corrections. Verify ambiguous original dates.
input_policy: All rows processed in one combined table; no origin-based data subsets are created.
limitations: Retrospective assessment of completed innings; no next-match forecasting.
Performance_Label is a researcher-defined rubric, not independent coach ground truth.
Classification scores measure agreement with that rubric, not coaching effectiveness.
The workbook records supplied and generated innings. All rows are processed together; scores are an internal mixed-data benchmark, not verified-real-world accuracy.
Dismissal-only context lacks successful deliveries faced; patterns are review candidates, not per-ball dismissal risks or proven technical faults.
Practice tips are evidence-linked suggestions from a fixed rule catalogue, not learned or coach-validated prescriptions.

rubric.T20: Poor: runs < 15; Good: runs >= 30 and SR >= 120; Average: otherwise.
rubric.ODI: Poor: runs < 20; Good: runs >= 50 and SR >= 80; Average: otherwise.
rubric.Test: Poor: runs < 20; Good: runs >= 50; Average: otherwise. SR is not used.
rubric.zero_balls: SR is encoded as 0; a zero-run run-out receives Poor as a scoring outcome, not a technical judgment.
